back: Rotates the plane of plane-polarised light; enantiomers rotate it by equal angles in opposite directions.

front: Why HCN addition to an aldehyde gives a racemate
back: The C=O carbon is planar, so CN⁻ attacks either face with equal probability.

front: Stereochemical result of SN2 on a chiral centre
back: Inversion of configuration: one enantiomer gives a single enantiomer of the product.
